exposure: High-risk pregnancy conditions (pregnancy-induced hypertension, eclampsia, diabetes, intrauterine growth restriction, thyroid disorder, heart disease, anemia, bad obstetric history, oligohydramnios, post-dated pregnancy, diminished fetal movements, premature rupture of membranes)
cohort: The study included 100 high-risk pregnant patients with a gestational age of >= 36 weeks.
finding: Abnormal antepartum CTG results were significantly associated with a higher rate of caesarean section, lower birth weight, and lower APGAR scores at one minute, suggesting CTG's effectiveness as a fetal monitoring screening technique.
mod_finding: Abnormal CTG results showed a significant association with caesarean section deliveries, accounting for 92.6% of caesarean sections among those with abnormal CTG.
birth_weight: Babies' birth weights were measured and categorized as less than 2.5 kg and over 2.5 kg for analysis.
